claim.quote: The T2K experiment observes indications of νμ→νe appearance in data accumulated with 1.43×10²⁰ protons on target. Six events pass all selection criteria at the far detector. ... the probability to observe six or more candidate events is 7×10⁻³, equivalent to 2.5σ significance.

date.note: arXiv submission June 2011; published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 107, 041801 (2011).

key_value_text.quote: At 90% C.L., the data are consistent with 0.03(0.04)<sin^2 2θ_13< 0.28(0.34) for δCP=0 and a normal (inverted) hierarchy.
key_value_text.value: sin^2(2 theta_13) consistent with 0.03(0.04) to 0.28(0.34) at 90% CL for normal (inverted) hierarchy, delta_CP = 0.

name: T2K indication of electron-neutrino appearance

summary.plain: In 2011, T2K saw the first hints that muon neutrinos can turn into electron neutrinos on their way across Japan - six candidate events where fewer than two were expected. It was not yet a firm discovery, just a tantalising early sign.
summary.technical: Six candidate nu_e-appearance events observed at Super-Kamiokande with 1.43e20 protons on target, against an expected background of 1.5+/-0.3 events; probability of a background-only fluctuation 7e-3 (2.5 sigma). Constrains sin^2(2 theta_13) to 0.03(0.04)-0.28(0.34) at 90% CL. The collaboration's own title says 'indication', a weaker claim than 'evidence' or 'observation'; classified here as result_type 'measurement' because the ontology's result_type enum has no 'indication' tier and 2.5 sigma is below the conventional ~3 sigma evidence threshold.

title: Indication of Electron Neutrino Appearance from an Accelerator-produced Off-axis Muon Neutrino Beam
why_it_matters: The first experimental hint, from any experiment, that theta_13 might be non-zero and that muon-to-electron neutrino appearance is observable at an accelerator; motivated the reactor experiments (Daya Bay, RENO, Double Chooz) that soon confirmed theta_13 != 0, and set up T2K's own later observation (2014) and CP-violation search (2020).
